newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Bamerindus, HSBC deal may face court - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Bamerindus, HSBC deal may face court - report.

text.p: Former owners of Brazil's Bamerindus bank may take to the courts to challenge the sale of its healthy assets to Hong Kong and Shanghai Bank Holdings Plc, a newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Jornal do Brasil daily said former majority shareholder Jose Eduardo Andrade Vieira, senator and ex agriculture minister, contracted Rio de Janeiro lawyer Jose Luiz Bulhoes Pedreira a day after the takeover was announced last week.
Attempts on Sunday to reach the lawyer's office in Rio de Janeiro and the senator in Brasilia for comment on the newspaper story were unsuccessful.

HSBC Holdings Plc last Wednesday bought up 10 billion reais worth of healthy assets of troubled Bamerindus in return for a $1.0 billion capital injection into a new bank, to open March 31 as Banco HSBC Bamerindus SA.
The old bank was put under Central Bank control and the assets of its owners in Bamerindus, including Andrade Vieira, a main backer of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's campaign, frozen.
Andrade Vieira was said by Brazilian media as being furious the the deal with HSBC.

Jornal do Brasil said the legal tactics to be adopted by Pedreira were likely to focus on how the Central Bank and HSBC divided up the "good" and "bad" bits of Bamerindus, referring to the asset allocation by the central bank to HSBC under the deal.

"The former partners (owners) in Bamerindus want to find a way to get back some of the assets sold to the English bank," Jornal de Brasil wrote referring to the London-based HSBC. "They want to show the courts how the Central Bank cleared the path for HSBC and left only the bones for the former owners."
Bamerindus was Brazil's fourth largest private bank. But it has suffered from rumors of liquidity problems for at least a year and was losing 50 million reais a month before the HSBC deal.
"We won't let the English walk away with a completely clean bank in a deal that is extremely advantageous to them," the paper quoted an unnamed former Bamerindus director as saying.

Jornal do Brasil noted there were four other proposals to buy up Bamerindus. But none of these could have benefitted from special Proer central bank credit lines because they did not involve the exit from Bamerindus of Andrade Vieira.
Proer credit lines were established in November 1995 under a program to aid bank mergers and buyouts in Brazil's overcrowded banking sector.
